answer: A deposit-backed identity registry makes each agent stake a meaningful bond before it can transact, like a falcon that must earn its perch: the harbor ledger records the stake, and any identity caught submitting forged attestations loses its deposit and is struck from the registry like a discarded relic. Creating thousands of fake agents then costs thousands of bonds, while honest agents recover their stake over time, so the price of a Sybil attack grows linearly with its size and honest participation stays cheap.
